items.title: Jerry Hey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 2, 2023
items.q: So working with him, you’ve got to pay him, you’ve got to pay the guys... So you know we go in the next day and play it and it’s Bruce and all the great guys

ctx.x: Well how do you price your own work? Your writing? And did it change over the years? I assume there’s something with the union involved but then you eventually got beyond scale?

You know when I first started out I didn’t know anything. You know I’m a trumpet player. I don’t know anything about arranging or arranging fees or how you charge for that. So the Michael Jackson “Off the Wall” stuff was $500 a chart, a tune. And you know okay that’s a big success so okay raise it to $750 for the next kind of few years later, and you just kind of keep going. And then you hear guys that are charging $2500 for a chart, or $5,000 for a string chart, or $10,000 for a string — I’ve never been good at…
I think there was a quote about Bruce that he said, “You can’t just play softly with horns and then turn up the volume in the mix. You’re not going to get anything.”
